question: A quarry needs the total force, in newtons, applied by its whole feeder installation. Each pan's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 up to 9, one for each of its numbered drive steps. A pan has a mass of 171 kg, and each drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A frame carries 2 identical drives, a feeder carries 4 frames, and the installation runs 4 identical feeders. What total force, in N, does the installation apply?

A ferry terminal is rating a linkspan actuator. The span's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 9a + 20 = 0. The moving span has a mass of 65 kg, and the control room is at 19 degrees C. The actuator supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A counterweight chain adds 19 N to the actuator's load, and a guide roller then relieves 12 N. The terminal has 8 identical linkspans. What total load, in N, do the linkspans carry?

A ropeway works is setting up a tensioning drive. Two index wheels carry 384 teeth and 289 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to that number; the carriage has a mass of 91000 g, and the machine house is at 21 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and a return spring adds 14 N to its load. A tower carries 9 identical drives, and a standing pre-load of 1 N is added to the tower's combined load. The works has 4 identical towers. What total load, in N, do the towers carry?

A packaging plant launches cartons from a kicker. The carton's launch speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 1*x^2 + 6*x between x = 0 and x = 3, where x is the kicker index. A carton has a mass of 10000 g. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 4 kickers on a lane and then by the 5 lanes in a hall. A control latch adds 24 J to the hall's total, and the plant has 8 identical halls. What total energy, in J, does the plant hold?

A dockside vehicle ramp is being rated. The ramp carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the area under the curve 1*x^2 + 4*x between x = 0 and x = 4, where x is the lever index. The carriage has a mass of 187000 g, and the control cabin is at 15 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion; a guide shoe relieves 21 N of it, and a seal relieves a further 19 N. The remainder is expressed in kilonewtons, and a standing frame relief of 14 kN is then subtracted. What is the net figure, in kN?

A mine needs the total force, in newtons, applied across its whole hoisting section. Each skip's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the larger value satisfying a^2 - 12a + 35 = 0. A skip has a mass of 198 kg, and the hoist supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A rope guide adds 15 N to the hoist's load. A shaft carries 9 identical hoists, the mine has 12 identical shafts, and a standing frame relief of 24 N is then taken off the mine's combined figure. What total force, in N, does the hoisting section apply?

A bottling plant needs the net figure, in newtons, for its whole capping section. Each capper head has 12 mounting bosses, and its carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to the number of distinct pairs of bosses that a brace could join. A carriage has a mass of 59 kg, and each head supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A machine carries 8 identical heads, a line runs 11 machines, and the plant has 12 identical lines. A standing frame relief of 30 N is then taken off the plant's combined figure. What is the net figure, in N?

A skittle-alley manufacturer tests a ball-return kicker. The ball's launch speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 4*x^2 + 3*x between x = 1 and x = 3, where x is the kicker-tension index. The ball has a mass of 14000 g, and the alley is at 20 degrees C. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules, and a standing rig allowance of 3 kJ is subtracted from it. The manufacturer tests 5 identical kickers. What total figure, in kJ, do the kickers show?

A dockyard needs the net figure, in kilonewtons, for a slipway winch. The base rate b, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying b^2 - 15*b + 56 = 0, and the gearbox drives the cradle at 10 times that base rate. The cradle has a mass of 163000 g, and the winch supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. That force is expressed in kilonewtons. A standing frame relief of 13 kN is then subtracted from it. What is the net figure, in kN?

A go-kart workshop tests a launch dolly on a short rail. The base value b is the smaller solution of b^2 - 8*b + 12 = 0, the gearbox multiplies it by 7, and a drag correction then takes 5 away, giving the dolly's speed in metres per second. The dolly has a mass of 28000 g, and the workshop is at 22 degrees C. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. The workshop runs 2 identical rails. What total energy, in kJ, do the rails hold?

A trampoline-park laboratory measures a test mass on a level guide. The mass's speed v, in m/s, is the larger value that satisfies v^2 - 6v + 5 = 0. The test mass is 19000 g. The energy it carries by virtue of its motion is expressed in kilojoules and multiplied by the 5 guides in the rig. A standing instrument allowance of 22 kJ is then subtracted from the rig's figure. The laboratory runs 4 identical rigs. What is the laboratory's net figure, in kJ?

A crane works needs the total figure, in kilonewtons, for a hoist installation. The drum's position along its guide is, in metres, 2*t^3 + 3*t^2 with t in seconds, and the rating is taken at the instant t = 4 s by differentiating that position 2 times to give the carriage's rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 178 kg, and the machine house is at 18 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the result is expressed in kilonewtons. A tower carries 8 identical hoists, and the works has 11 identical towers. What total figure, in kN, does the installation show?

A ski-tow operator tests a tow bar on a straight run. The bar is brought up to speed by 3 identical drive stages, and each stage contributes 2 m/s as the clutch engages and a further 13 m/s as it drives, so the bar moves at the accumulated speed. The bar has a mass of 38000 g. From the energy it carries by virtue of that motion, 11 J is deducted for the guide friction and a further 11 J for the sheave drag. The result is expressed in kilojoules, and the tow carries 12 identical bars. What total energy, in kJ, does the tow hold?

A vibration bench drives a fixture whose acceleration, in metres per second squared, is set to twice the sum of its two dial readings, and both dials are turned to 8. The fixture on the bench has a mass of 24000 g, and a warning lamp on the bench is rated at 15 W. A second identical fixture is mounted on the opposite arm, so the drive must supply twice the push it supplied for one fixture. Expressed in kilonewtons, that combined push is doubled again when the bench is switched to its high-range mode. The bench's calibration report then subtracts a fixed 29 kN offset from the high-range figure. What number does the calibration report give, in kN?

A drop-hammer test cell launches a sled whose speed, in metres per second, is 3 times the sum of its two gate readings, and both gates read 3. The sled has a mass of 38000 g, and the cell's warning beacon draws 40 W. The cell fires 12 identical sleds in a batch, so the batch carries 12 times the energy of one sled. From the batch total the operator subtracts 1 J lost in the release latch, and then doubles what remains, because the rig runs a mirrored second bay firing the same batch. How much energy does the doubled figure represent, in kJ?

A workshop tests an electric winch that accelerates a sled of mass 82000 g along a level floor. The controller sets the sled's acceleration in metres per second squared to a value whose square, minus 6 times the value, plus 5, is exactly 0, and the workshop uses the larger of the two values that satisfy this. The winch has 5 identical drums pulling in parallel, so the total pull is 5 times the pull on the single sled, expressed in kilonewtons. The safety report then subtracts 2 kN for the anchor allowance and a further 5 kN for the floor-bolt allowance. What figure does the safety report end with, in kN?

A structures lab closes its report with a value obtained by taking 12 times an intermediate margin and then subtracting a further 16 kN for the reaction frame. The intermediate margin is the force driving the test mass, expressed in kilonewtons, minus 16 kN allowed for the fixture's own weight. The test mass is 104000 g, and it is accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, of 7 times the sum of the two ramp settings, which read 4 and 5. The lab repeats this closing calculation after every rebuild of the rig. What value does the lab's report close with, in kN?

A test loop's report ends with a number found by taking a certain kilojoule figure, subtracting 16 and then adding 8. That kilojoule figure is the kinetic energy of a 48 kg trolley on the loop, expressed in kilojoules. The trolley's speed in metres per second equals a certain accumulated meter total, minus 18. That accumulated total is what the loop's meter registers between the 3rd and the 4th second of a run, while the instantaneous rate it registers at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 2 times t. What number does the report end with, in kJ?

A conveyor audit finishes by multiplying a certain energy balance by 9. That balance is the kinetic energy of the shuttle expressed in kilojoules, less 27 kJ charged to the drive cabinet and a further 26 kJ charged to the chiller. The shuttle has a mass of 30 kg. Its distance travelled along the rail, in metres, is 5 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds minus 2 times the square of that time, and the audit uses how fast the shuttle is moving at the instant 1 second after release. What figure does the audit finish with, in kJ?

A packing line handles 139 tins on one belt and 140 tins on the other, and the supervisor forms identical trays using the largest tray size that divides both counts exactly. The line's test puck has a mass of 36000 g and travels at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that tray size. The line runs 10 pucks per lane, there are 5 lanes on the floor, and the plant operates 6 identical floors. A status lamp on each floor draws 18 W. How much kinetic energy do all the pucks in the plant carry at once, in kJ?

A depot ships 250 crates of one kind and 234 of another, and the loader stacks them into identical columns using the largest column height that divides both totals exactly. A test cart is then sent down the ramp at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that column height plus 27. The cart has a mass of 41000 g, and the ramp is lit by a 60 W lamp. The energy audit takes the cart's kinetic energy in kilojoules, subtracts 23 kJ booked to the hoist and then a further 6 kJ booked to the door motor. What does the energy audit report, in kJ?

A bicycle workshop receives 395 spokes of one gauge and 253 of another, and it bundles them into identical packs using the largest pack size that divides both counts exactly. The workshop's test dummy has a mass of 77000 g and is pushed along the rig at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pack size. Two such dummies are pushed together on one rig, so the rig's drive supplies twice the force needed for one. The logged figure then subtracts 22 N for the trolley bearings, and the workshop runs 10 identical rigs side by side. What total force do the 10 rigs log, in N?

A crane test ends with a reading equal to 4 times a corrected force, because four identical hoists share the same duty. The corrected force is the force acting on the test block, reduced by 18 N for sheave friction and then increased by 1 N for the load-cell offset. The block has a mass of 54 kg. Its upward speed, in metres per second, is 1 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds minus 2 times the square of that time, and the test is read at the instant 2 seconds into the lift, using how fast that speed is changing at that moment. What reading does the crane test end with, in N?

A demolition contractor's estimate is 8 times the energy of one district's programme, and each district runs 3 identical sites. A site's programme is the energy of a single swing plus 6 J for the release gear, expressed in kilojoules. The wrecking ball has a mass of 52000 g. Its speed at the bottom of the swing, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the 13 anchor points on the frame, taking 2 at a time. What is the contractor's estimate, in kJ?

A rally team's energy sheet ends by adding 30 J for the starter motor and then subtracting 18 J for the telemetry unit. Before those two adjustments the sheet holds 6 times the kinetic energy of one test sled, because six sleds run the course together. Each sled has a mass of 57 kg, and the course is 250 m long. A sled's speed, in metres per second, is 7 times the largest whole number that divides both 75 and 91 exactly. What figure does the energy sheet end with, in J?
